tonight.headline: Sadiq is still a Sunday-morning call, and the flex is still a point off
body: The bad news is the same as last night's. Kenyon Sadiq, your only tight end, was limited all three days with his back and is questionable; no coach has said which way it leans, and nothing new was reported by 07:00 this morning. The Ravens D/ST are without Trey Hendrickson. ESPN has you at 123.1 against Team 13's 88.3, 68%, because their lineup still carries two players who are ruled out.

Two things before Sunday. The flex still has Tuten where the projection prefers Downs by a point: a coin flip, so take the projection, before 07:30 tomorrow (card 1). One correction strengthens it: Keenan Allen didn't practise on Friday, where last night's brief said limited. And at 09:30 tomorrow check the Jets' inactives: if Sadiq is out, Mark Andrews is still a free agent with no game status.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Team 13 still start DeVonta Smith and Rachaad White, both ruled out (NFL.com status list), at 0.0 each, with Kyle Pitts (7.4) at tight end and Travis Kelce in the flex. On their bench: DJ Moore 13.0, Dalton Kincaid 10.7, Blake Corum 8.1 and Lamar Jackson, who is off Baltimore's report. Josh Allen has no designation.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 moving Moore and Corum in for Smith and White: about 21 projected points back, which takes 88.3 to roughly 109 and the gap to about 14.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sun 07:30 Mexico City (Downs locks in London)
doFirst.title: Put Downs back in the flex over Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: 13.7 to 12.7. Carried for a fifth run and still not done. A coin flip, so it goes to the projection — and no thesis.

case.label: The rule
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'start Josh Downs 13.7 over Bhayshul Tuten 12.7 — COIN FLIP, take the projection.' Neither has a game status: Indianapolis list only Keenan Allen and Ashton Dulin, both questionable, and Jacksonville list three defenders (NFL.com status list, re-read 3 Oct).

case.label: The player
case.body: Downs drew 11 targets in Week 3, a third of Indianapolis' (archive), with Pierce on IR. Keenan Allen was limited Wednesday and Thursday and then did not practise on Friday; RotoWire says his groin 'moved the wrong direction' (ProFootballTalk; RotoWire 2 Oct). Last night's brief called it three limited days; that was wrong. If Allen sits, Downs' share grows, and that isn't in the 13.7. Washington have allowed the most points to receivers (footballdb, standard scoring).

case.label: The timing cost
case.body: Downs locks at 07:30 tomorrow in London, Tuten at 11:00. Putting Downs in the flex gives up a little late flexibility, but nothing on this roster is waiting on a later inactive except Sadiq, and only a tight end covers him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tuten outscores Downs. It's a coin flip: this is the expected-value call, not a prediction, and it gets no decision-log entry.

doFirst.sources: lineup_check.py · NFL.com · ProFootballTalk · RotoWire · footballdb · Week 3 archive

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · if Sadiq is inactive at Sun 09:30 Mexico City; both lock at 11:00
doFirst.title: If Sadiq sits: add Mark Andrews, drop Carnell Tate
doFirst.subtitle: Carried, unchanged overnight: Sadiq is questionable, not out. Andrews is still a free agent, so it's an add with no priority cost.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Sadiq hurt his back on a diving touchdown catch in Week 3 and was limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; he's questionable (NewYorkJets.com Friday report, read directly this morning). No coach has spoken to his availability and nothing dated Saturday existed at 07:00. Mason Taylor (thumb) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) are ruled out, so if he plays the role is large; Jeremy Ruckert (knee) practised in full Friday and is the Jets' other healthy tight end. ESPN: QUESTIONABLE at 9.9.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: Andrews projects 10.1 at home to Tennessee and isn't among Baltimore's statuses (NFL.com status list; BaltimoreRavens.com 2 Oct). 6, 7, 5 targets (archive). Zay Flowers is questionable with a hamstring listing after a limited Friday the Ravens call rest. He's a FREEAGENT in this snapshot: an add, not a claim, and anyone else can make it first. If he's gone: Hockenson (9.1, 14:05) or Darren Waller (9.3), who plays Sunday night against the defence allowing the most points to tight ends.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Carnell Tate, the fifth receiver and not on the screen's exposure list. Kamara and Gordon are on it, and Golden and Downs both project above him, so none of them is the drop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Andrews scores less than the best free tight end that week (Hunter Henry, Loveland).

whatWentWrong.title: The flex has sat a point below the projection since Wednesday night
whatWentWrong.lead: Downs went into the flex at 14:10 Wednesday and back out for Tuten at 21:31 that night, Mexico City time. Five briefs later it hasn't moved.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Section 0 of the strategy: every Week 1–2 loss was winnable with the roster owned, and the most expensive mistake was overriding the projection. A one-point flip isn't a disaster; the habit is.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: News ESPN hasn't priced about Downs or Tuten. The one new item cuts toward Downs: Keenan Allen missed Friday's practice.

whatWentWrong.sources: ESPN activity log · STRATEGY.md · NFL.com · ProFootballTalk

whatWentWrong.title: One tight end, limited three days running and questionable
whatWentWrong.lead: Back injury, limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. No bench player can cover the slot.

case.label: The tool
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'NOBODY ELIGIBLE on the bench — find one on the wire.' That's the Andrews card.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Sadiq active at 09:30 tomorrow: nothing fires. A downgrade to doubtful or out today: make the Andrews add then rather than waiting.

worthALook.name: Bills D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison: the Bills are free at 8.0 and the Ravens are at 7.0. Still a hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Bills 8.0 at home to New England, who rule out Gonzalez and Barmore on defence; Drake Maye plays (a CBS headline: 'Good to go for Week 4'), having taken 12 sacks and turned it over 7 times in three games (Yahoo 29 Sep). Ravens 7.0 at home to Tennessee without Trey Hendrickson, against a Titans line that lost two guards to IR this week (AtoZ Sports 2 Oct). The Steelers, 8.2 on paper, played Thursday.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: The gap is exactly 1.0: inside the two-point coin-flip line, and the D/ST seat changed hands on Wednesday. The churn rule closes a seat for seven days unless the player in it is ruled out. A defence missing one rusher isn't ruled out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Ravens' number falling two points below a free defence that hasn't kicked off.

worthALook.sources: ESPN · BaltimoreRavens.com · AtoZ Sports · CBS · Yahoo · STRATEGY.md

worthALook.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison: 0.1 better than Myers and a free agent. Hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Fairbairn 9.8, Myers 9.7. He's a free agent and costs no priority, but the kicker seat changed hands on Wednesday and a tenth of a point isn't a reason to change it again. Neither is on his team's final report (NFL.com status list; Seahawks.com 2 Oct). The Chargers have allowed the 10th-most kicker points (footballdb, three weeks).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers appearing on Seattle's report.

doNotChase.name: Dontayvion Wicks
doNotChase.lead: The wire's biggest riser: Philadelphia's top receiver for a week, and still below your fifth.

case.label: The rise
case.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) are ruled out, and the Eagles will use Wicks as their top receiver against the Rams; the staff were 'extremely impressed' by his week as the primary target (NBC Sports Philadelphia 3 Oct). 4, 6, 5 targets for 15.3, 12.4 and 5.2 points (archive).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 11.2, below Tate (11.9), the fifth receiver on a roster that starts two plus a flex. The vacancy is one week unless Smith's hamstring lingers, and the Eagles' own columnist expects them to run it through Barkley (The Inquirer 3 Oct).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight-plus targets tomorrow with Smith missing a second game: then he's compared with Tate on Tuesday. He's a free agent, so no priority is at stake.

doNotChase.sources: Week 1–3 archive · NBC Sports Philadelphia · The Inquirer · NFL.com

doNotChase.name: Darren Waller
doNotChase.lead: A rising tight end: tempting with Sadiq questionable, and still third in line.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 8 targets and 10.1 points in Week 3 (archive), most of it after Jalen Coker left with a quad injury. Coker is questionable and a game-day decision (Yahoo 2 Oct); Xavier Legette is out. Waller himself has no game status (NFL.com status list).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 9.3, below Andrews (10.1) and Sadiq (9.9), and adding him today costs a roster seat for a player who doesn't start unless Sadiq sits. 2 and 3 targets in Weeks 1–2 (archive): the role appeared when Coker left and may leave when he returns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Sadiq inactive at 09:30 tomorrow with Andrews already taken: then Waller is a live fallback, because he plays Sunday night against Detroit, who allow the most points to tight ends (footballdb), and stays addable all afternoon.

doNotChase.sources: Week 1–3 archive · Yahoo · NFL.com · footballdb · ESPN

doNotChase.name: George Holani
doNotChase.lead: New on the list: Seattle's rookie starter is out, and Holani is the smaller half of what's left.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Jadarian Price re-aggravated a chest injury in practice and is ruled out; Macdonald: 'I'm not sure how long he's going to be out.' Seahawks.com says Holani and Emanuel Wilson 'will carry the load' against the Chargers (2 Oct). Holani caught 5 of 5 targets for 48 yards in Week 3 (archive).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 8, 4, 3 carries against Wilson's 2, 21, 9 (archive); SI projects the split at about 60% Wilson, 35% Holani, with Wilson ahead 9 to 6 in red-zone carries (2 Oct). Wilson is rostered here by Los Cachanillas. Zach Charbonnet is eligible to come off PUP in Week 5 (Seahawks.com), and KEI returns hold him. Holani projects 10.4, a shade under Kamara (10.6), already on your bench.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Holani out-carrying Wilson tomorrow with Price still out next week and Charbonnet not activated.

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Cleared for Sunday after two full practices; he's splitting the backfield you spent priority on.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Full Thursday and Friday, no designation (NFL.com status list). Hafley: 'should be good to go'. Fowler: the two 'will share the load in the short term' (SI 2 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be a fifth back on a roster that starts two, at Minnesota, who allow the 4th-fewest points to RBs (footballdb) and haven't let a back reach 50 rushing yards or score (SI 2 Oct). 3 carries all season (archive). A free agent, but a roster seat is still a cost. ESPN: 7.5 to Gordon's 9.0.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over Miami outright tomorrow (Gordon under 8 touches) — then Gordon is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.name: Kendre Miller
doNotChase.lead: The other half of a backfield you already own, and it may be a third.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Travis Etienne went on IR, and Kellen Moore said 'Alvin and Kendre will handle that load really well' (carried). After the injury the Week 3 carries went Kamara 6, Miller 4 (Yahoo 2 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 4 carries and 3 targets for 3.9 points in Week 3 (archive). Yahoo reads it as a three-way split, with CJ Donaldson taking the goal line. You own Kamara, who projects 10.6 to Miller's 8.8 and still sits on your bench.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Miller out-touching Kamara on Monday night: then Kamara is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage, from three weeks of data, which is still thin. The only wire need is the Sadiq fallback, an injury plan rather than a usage gap.
